We are Ctrl Win, a team of university students interested in technology, space, and sustainability.

Our project focuses on "Adapting Farms with NASA Data", aiming to use NASA data to help farmers adapt to climate change and improve agriculture.

ke informed decisions with ease.

details:
TerraScope – An Intelligent Platform for Agricultural Decision Support

TerraScope is an intelligent agricultural platform designed to help farmers make better farming decisions based on NASA Earth observation and satellite data.

The core idea behind the project is to answer an important question that every farmer faces:

“What should I plant after my current crop, based on the condition of my land and the surrounding environmental conditions?”

How Does the Project Work?

TerraScope relies on analyzing satellite data and environmental indicators to understand the condition of agricultural land, including soil moisture, rainfall rates, vegetation health, and environmental and climatic changes.

Users enter some basic information, such as the location and area of their land, as well as the crop currently being cultivated. The platform then uses available environmental data to assess the land’s condition and suggest crops that may be suitable for cultivation in the upcoming season.

To ensure that farmers do not have to deal with complex scientific data and figures, the platform simplifies the analysis results and transforms them into clear, practical, and easy-to-understand recommendations.

Key Features

  • Agricultural Land Analysis: Provides insights into land conditions using environmental indicators and data.
  • Crop Recommendations: Helps farmers choose the most suitable crop to plant after their current harvest.
  • Environmental Monitoring: Uses satellite data to track environmental changes that may affect agricultural activities.
  • User-Friendly Interface: Designed in Arabic, using simple Egyptian dialect, to make the platform accessible to farmers, including those with limited technological experience.
  • AI-Powered Agricultural Assistant: Features a virtual character named “Am Magdy”, who acts as an agricultural assistant, explaining analysis results and answering farmers’ questions in a simple and relatable way.

Project Goals and Benefits

TerraScope aims to:

  • Help farmers make data-driven agricultural decisions instead of relying entirely on guesswork.
  • Reduce the risks of cultivating crops that are unsuitable for current environmental conditions.
  • Contribute to better utilization of agricultural land and water resources.
  • Make NASA’s scientific data more accessible and valuable to farming communities.
  • Promote sustainable agriculture and help address the challenges of climate change and water scarcity.
  • Contribute to strengthening food security by improving agricultural production decisions.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using a combination of tools and technologies, including:

  • NASA Earth Observation Data: NASA’s Earth observation and satellite data, used to analyze environmental and agricultural indicators.
  • HTML: Used to build the website’s basic structure.
  • CSS: Used to design the user interface and enhance the overall user experience.
  • JavaScript: Used to implement interactive features and data-processing functions within the website.
  • Google AI Studio: Used to help develop the intelligent agricultural assistant and enable it to interact with users’ questions.
  • Web Hosting: Used to deploy the platform online and make it accessible to users.

Expected Project Impact

TerraScope seeks to bridge the gap between space technology and the everyday needs of farmers by transforming complex scientific data provided by satellites into simple, practical, and actionable agricultural insights.

Our vision is for TerraScope to become a tool that helps farmers better understand their land, make more informed decisions, preserve natural resources, and contribute to building a more sustainable agricultural future.
